norm_rules.text: Pagar solo si el NIF esta en el maestro y el IBAN de la factura coincide con el maestro.

checks.text: The invoice's `issuer_nif` (normalised) must appear as `suppliers.nif` (normalised) in the suppliers master.
checks.kind_reason: The data is present and the NIF is absent from the master, which clearly breaks the payment condition.
checks.interpretation: I read 'el NIF esta en el maestro' as the invoice's issuer_nif matching a suppliers.nif row after normalisation; the sentence names no outcome for this failure, so it is a policy check.

checks.text: The invoice's `iban` (normalised) must equal the `suppliers.iban` (normalised) of the supplier whose `suppliers.nif` (normalised) equals the invoice's `issuer_nif` (normalised).
checks.kind_reason: The invoice IBAN is present and differs from the master's IBAN for that supplier, a clear breach of the payment condition.
checks.interpretation: I read 'el IBAN de la factura coincide con el maestro' as comparing the invoice iban with the suppliers.iban of the matched supplier row; no outcome is named, so it is a policy check.

policies: Pagar solo si se cumplen las condiciones: la frase fija la condición de pago, no el resultado de su incumplimiento.

norm_rules.text: El pedido debe existir, pertenecer al proveedor y el importe de la factura debe ser igual al del pedido (tolerancia 0,01 EUR).

checks.kind_reason: The order reference is present but no matching order row exists, which clearly breaks the condition.
checks.interpretation: I read 'el pedido debe existir' as the invoice purchase_order matching an orders row; no outcome is named, so it is a policy check.

checks.text: The order found for the invoice's `purchase_order` must belong to the supplier: `orders.supplier_id` must equal the `suppliers.id` of the supplier whose `suppliers.nif` (normalised) equals the invoice's `issuer_nif` (normalised).
checks.kind_reason: The order exists and its supplier_id differs from the invoice issuer's supplier, a clear breach of the condition.
checks.interpretation: I read 'pertenecer al proveedor' as the order's supplier_id matching the supplier identified by the invoice's issuer_nif; no outcome is named, so it is a policy check.

checks.text: The invoice's `total` must match the order's `orders.total_amount` within ±0.01 EUR (abs(cents(total) - cents(total_amount)) <= 1).
checks.kind_reason: Both amounts are present and differ beyond the tolerance, a clear breach of the condition.
checks.interpretation: I read 'el importe de la factura debe ser igual al del pedido' as the invoice total compared with orders.total_amount with the stated 0.01 EUR tolerance; no outcome is named, so it is a policy check.

norm_rules.text: El IVA debe estar bien calculado y el total debe ser base + IVA, con la misma tolerancia de 0,01 EUR.

checks.text: The invoice's `vat_amount` must match `base` * `vat_rate` / 100 within ±0.01 EUR (abs(cents(vat_amount) - cents(base * vat_rate / 100)) <= 1).
checks.kind_reason: Base, rate and VAT amount are present and the VAT is miscalculated, a clear breach of the condition.
checks.interpretation: I read 'el IVA debe estar bien calculado' as vat_amount equalling base times vat_rate (a percentage) with the 0.01 EUR tolerance; no outcome is named, so it is a policy check.

checks.text: The invoice's `total` must match `base` + `vat_amount` within ±0.01 EUR (abs(cents(total) - cents(base + vat_amount)) <= 1).
checks.kind_reason: Base, VAT and total are present and the total does not equal base + VAT, a clear breach of the condition.
checks.interpretation: I read 'el total debe ser base + IVA' as total equalling base plus vat_amount with the same 0.01 EUR tolerance; no outcome is named, so it is a policy check.

norm_rules.text: La fecha debe ser valida y no futura.

checks.text: The invoice's `date` must be a valid calendar date (a real YYYY-MM-DD day, e.g. not 2026-02-31).
checks.kind_reason: The date is present and impossible, which clearly breaks the condition.
checks.interpretation: I read 'la fecha debe ser valida' as the invoice date being a real calendar date; no outcome is named, so it is a policy check.

checks.text: The invoice's `date` must not be later than `parameters.cut_off_date` (compared as dates).
checks.kind_reason: The date is present and after the cut-off, a clear breach of the condition.
checks.interpretation: I read 'no futura' as the invoice date not exceeding the process cut-off date from parameters; no outcome is named, so it is a policy check.

norm_rules.text: Estado ERP del pedido: PENDIENTE. Nunca pagar dos veces el mismo pedido.

checks.text: The `erp` entry of the invoice's `purchase_order` (normalised) must have `erp.status` = 'PENDIENTE'.
checks.kind_reason: The ERP entry exists and its status is not PENDIENTE, a clear breach of the condition.
checks.interpretation: I read 'Estado ERP del pedido: PENDIENTE' as the erp row for the invoice's purchase_order having status PENDIENTE; no outcome is named, so it is a policy check.

checks.text: The `erp` entry of the invoice's `purchase_order` (normalised) must not have `erp.status` = 'PAGADA' (the order must not already be paid).
checks.kind_reason: The external ERP record shows the order already paid, which clearly proves paying again would be wrong.
checks.interpretation: I read 'Nunca pagar dos veces el mismo pedido' as forbidding payment when the erp record of the order already shows status PAGADA; no outcome is named, so it is a policy check.

checks.text: No other instance in `others` may carry the same normalised `purchase_order` as this invoice.
checks.kind_reason: Several instances share an order reference that should be unique, so the system cannot tell which invoice is legitimate and a person must decide.
checks.interpretation: I read 'Nunca pagar dos veces el mismo pedido' as also covering duplicate invoices for the same order across instances; since the system cannot tell which is legitimate, this is a doubt check.

norm_rules.text: Cualquier anomalia que un humano deba ver: ESCALAR con motivo. Ante duda razonable, escalar antes que pagar.
policies: Cualquier anomalia que un humano deba ver se ESCALA con motivo.
Ante duda razonable, escalar antes que pagar.
